analysis: Examined the changed regions in ClusterService.swift (provider-swift/Sources/ProviderCore/Inference/Distributed/Onboarding/ClusterService.swift). The visible patch hunks are mechanical rewrites of date comparisons: `Date() >= x` becomes `Date().timeIntervalSince(x) >= 0` at the memory-replan gate (line 510), syncMembers gate (646), the stopLocalPart deadline check (909), checkForUpdate (1044) and checkApproval (1126). A sixth changed line (1582) is outside the supplied excerpts and could not be reviewed; the patch excerpt is truncated. The rewrites keep the same semantics: Date >= Date is equivalent to timeIntervalSince >= 0 for finite dates. They do not alter authorization, pairing-pin checks (`pairing.peerPin == leadership.peerPin`), claim supersession checks, command-lock acquisition, or the token/credential handling. The one difference is that if a date were `distantPast` or `distantFuture`, timeIntervalSince returns large finite values, so nextStart/nextApprovalCheck = .distantPast still compares >= 0 as true. No new attack surface, no change to the trust boundaries TB-002/TB-011, and no change to the encryption, cache (T-041) or attestation paths. Residual uncertainty is limited to the unseen change at base/head line 1582 and the truncated patch; neither is evidence of a regression.
